grh_6c805951c1514bacce14.title: Carousel
paragraphs: Carousel barker Billy Bigelow marries Julie but becomes desperate about providing for the child they are expecting and joins a robbery that ends with his death. In the afterlife Billy is offered one day back on earth to do something worthwhile and learns that his daughter Louise is now nearly twelve and burdened by her father's reputation. His attempt to help her is clumsy, but he gives Louise the courage to stop measuring herself by other people's judgment and urges her to meet the world without fear. Julie senses Billy's presence, and the visit leaves mother and daughter stronger than before.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Gordon MacRae, Norman Luboff, Nadine Conner, Julie Bennett, and Peter Leeds. Other credited names include Jerome Lawrence as radio adaptor, Robert E. Lee as radio adaptor, Gordon MacRae as host, and Marvin Miller as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.f7185f50dd01455d|Association of American Railroads]].
This version dramatizes [[work|work.rr.9ef0a58e7ec08d11|Carousel]]. Jerome Lawrence adapted it for radio and Robert E. Lee adapted it for radio.

grh_6c8e3d2977529557a654.title: Words at War 43-08-21 (10) Malta Spitfire
paragraphs: A dramatization of George F. Beurling and Leslie Roberts' Malta Spitfire traces Beurling from a Canadian boy obsessed with airplanes to a fighter pilot defending Malta. Rejected at first because he lacked the expected schooling, he persists until he reaches combat, where experience teaches the fiercely independent flyer that survival depends on teamwork as well as marksmanship. During the siege of Malta he helps defend vital convoys against Axis aircraft, is eventually shot down and badly wounded, and is presented as one of the young pilots whose endurance helped keep the island supplied and in Allied hands.

The cast includes Joseph Julian, Irene Hubbard, [[person|lon-clark|Lon Clark]], John Griggs, and Peter Hernandez. Other credited names include Joseph Losey as director and Kenneth White as radio adaptor.
The surviving recording runs about 31 minutes.
